title.narrative: Output 3.4. Increased capacity of Member States to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative: A total of 7,426 households and approximately 30,508 individuals benefitted from 56 infrastructure development in conflict-affected regions. These have provided essential services such as clean water, improved WASH facilities, education facilities, healthcare access, better roads, and enhanced connectivity through footbridges. This also created over 52,000 workdays of short-term employment that provided valuable income-generating opportunities for both men and women, contributing to greater economic empowerment and improved livelihoods. Women accounted for 49.29% of workdays, with access to social equity. The implementation of TVET programs bridged the skills gap and enhanced the employability of participants. With 397 individuals benefiting from these training courses, including 54% women. The ILO with funding from the Government of New Zealand injected NZD 1.2 million cash in the COVID and conflicts affected areas supported local economic development, job creation while improving the living conditions for the community. The ILO with the support from New Zealand government helped to establish 48 Village Infrastructure Operation and Maintenance Committee (VIOMC) to ensure the sustainability of the infrastructure in those villages. The ILO provided technical support to members of the VIOMC to support them in performing their roles well. Moreover, 48 Village Development Committees were also formed and trained by the ILO. The ILO successfully conducted training programs for all 48 VDCs, equipping them with the necessary knowledge and skills to effectively fulfill their roles and responsibilities. This training played a crucial role in ensuring smooth implementation while upholding principles according to the International Humanitarian Law within the areas controlled by the Ethnic Armed Organizations (EAOs). The trained VDCs played a pivotal role in facilitating solutions to problems in implementation. The VDC’s enhanced capabilities and understanding of their roles enabled them to effectively manage activities, address any challenges that arose, and ensure that resources were allocated and utilized efficiently. The training also fostered a sense of ownership among the VDCs, as they became active participants in decision-making processes. The ILO with funding support from the New Zealand government also trained 56 community contractors on construction contract management. The training equipped them with the necessary skills and knowledge to effectively carry out their roles and responsibilities. A key factor for success was the close collaboration between the community contractors and the Village Development Committees (VDCs). They worked hand in hand, making collective management decisions to ensure transparency and accountability towards the relevant communities. The community contractors, along with the VDCs, actively engaged in decision-making processes, addressing community needs and concerns throughout the implementation.

Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: Partner organizations/trainers sustained the conduct of training programmes benefitting over 2,000 (potential) entrepreneurs covering productivity, OSH, responsible business practices, and enterprise development, including environmentally sustainable practices using ILO approaches. These include the following: 1) Start and Improve Your Business(SIYB) training, Leht Li Business Skills training and “Are Thit” training with Coca Cola Company and Business Eye Opener (BEO). 2) As part of SCORE sustainability, SCORE Expert Trainers developed business plans for sales and delivery of ToT. According to 9 Expert Trainers’ business plan, 20 ToTs delivered SCORE and SCORE HoCo with 40 trainers without any further financial and technical support between 2022-June 2023. Around 30 (54% Women) new trainers are certified SCORE training and HoCo in 2022- June 2023. From 2022 to June 2023, 2,300 staffs from 83 enterprises in manufacturing and tourism achieved SCORE/SCORE HoCo methodologies. 3) SIYB trainers provided GYB-SYB training under cash-for-training programme to 91 unemployed workers in garment sector. 4) 6 SCORE trainers and 2 SCORE Expert Trainers trained around 200 OSH focal from 19 garment factories. 5) Helvetas and SIYB Master Trainers trained around 30 Potential/Existing entrepreneurs through Business Management Training. 6) Prevent Plastics Myanmar’s 7 SCORE Trainers delivered waste management training, derived from SCORE Resource Efficiency and Cleaner Production Module, successfully delivered to 8377 participants (5,463 female) in 452 trainings at 450 factories. 7) Expert Trainers organized 7 SCORE promotion events in Mandalay and Shan State with 180 participants (SMEs), using the 5 case studies. With support from the Switzerland and Norway, the ILO continues to support private sector freelance trainers and training companies that assist MSMEs in Myanmar. The ILO has provided technical support to Expert Trainers to develop business plans for sales and delivery of Training on Trainers (ToT) and continue support trainers certification, monitoring and evaluation and develop the quality assurance system for SCORE in Myanmar. Support is provided for training modules revision to meet SME needs and developed case studies to feature the benefits of SCORE Training to be used as promotional materials for attracting new participants. Organize meetings with lead buyers to enhance understanding of advanced supplier development practices, incorporating concepts of cooperation in the workspace, gender equality and working conditions. Coordinate to integrate the training (SCORE/SME Training) and support to extend network and enhance impacts for Decent work. The ILO developed 5 case studies to feature the benefits of SCORE Training, were used as promotional materials to attract new training participants. ILO promoted SCORE through these materials in social media including Facebook and LinkedIn etc;
